ANT 101.title: Introduction to Anesthesia Technology
notices: Taken from the College of Healthcare Technology curriculum (Anesthesia Technology, Appendices VII and VIII). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
ANT 101.description: This course is an introduction to the basics of the anesthesia specialty, including general, regional, and sedation anesthesia. It explores the history of non-physician anesthesia, ethical considerations, and legal aspects governing the profession, as well as the scope of practice of anesthesia technologists, their duties and responsibilities in the healthcare setting and their relationship with other healthcare professionals. Moreover, the course outlines the standard of care and procedural requirements in anesthesia practice. Students will also acquire a fundamental knowledge of the anesthesia equipment, surgical anesthesia environment, and workplace management and safety. Prerequisite: None.

ANT 240.title: Anesthesia Technology Instrumentation
notices: Taken from the College of Healthcare Technology curriculum (Anesthesia Technology, Appendices VII and VIII). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
ANT 240.description: This course focuses on familiarizing students with the equipment and instrumentation used in providing general, regional, and sedation anesthesia in both basic and complex situations. The anesthetic equipment described in this course includes but is not limited to the anesthesia machine, airway equipment, and ancillary anesthetic equipment including gas cylinders, ventilators, pulse oximetry, and absorbers. For every device described, mechanical and electrical characteristics of anesthesia delivery systems will be addressed, and students will learn how to set up, calibrate, operate, troubleshoot, maintain, and apply safety guidelines whilst using the devices. Prerequisites: ANT 101; BIO 217.

ANT 240L.title: Anesthesia Technology Instrumentation Lab
notices: Taken from the College of Healthcare Technology curriculum (Anesthesia Technology, Appendices VII and VIII). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
ANT 240L.description: This laboratory course is a hands-on and applied laboratory course provided concomitantly with the ANT 240 (Anesthesia Technology Instrumentation) didactic course. Prerequisites: ANT 101; BIO 217. Co-requisite: ANT 240.

ANT 245.title: Pharmacology in Anesthesia Practice
notices: Taken from the College of Healthcare Technology curriculum (Anesthesia Technology, Appendices VII and VIII). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
ANT 245.description: This course describes the relationship between pharmacology and physiology, drug mechanisms, pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics of anesthetic agents and analgesic agents, as well as their actions, interactions, and drug-receptor interactions. The course also focuses on the effects of anesthetic drugs on body systems pertinent to anesthetic procedures and practice, including the nervous, cardiovascular, and respiratory systems. Cases studies are included in the course material. Pharmacotherapy of anesthesia agents in specialized populations, including elderly and children will also be discussed. Prerequisite: CHE 105; BIO 217.

ANT 320.description: The purpose of this course is to impart in-depth information about the anesthesia management plan for the following anesthesia subspecialities: general, gastrointestinal, obstetric, gynecologic, and genitourinary. For each subspeciality, students will learn to prepare and implement an anesthetic plan in the cases of general, regional, and sedation anesthesia, and will acquire the kpnowledge related to the technique, anatomy, and pathophysiologic implications. ANT 330.description: This course details the procedures and set of standards required in the organization and maintenance of the anesthesia workplace throughout patient clinical monitoring. The course provides students with a working knowledge of devices and equipment used in real-time monitoring of patients under general, regional, or sedation anesthesia. Oxygenation, ventilation, temperature, urine output, hemodynamics, and neurological status are among the parameters that will be described about patient monitoring. Point- of-care testing and its more advanced technologies including Point-of-Care Ultrasound (POCUS) will also be addressed. Prerequisite: ANT 240; ANT 245. Co-requisite: ANT 340.

ANT 340.title: Anesthesia Agents and Methods
notices: Taken from the College of Healthcare Technology curriculum (Anesthesia Technology, Appendices VII and VIII). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
ANT 340.description: This course offers a complete overview of the various classes of anesthetic agents and analgesics pertaining to anesthesia. Calculation of dosages, physics gas laws, and routes of administration will be addressed in detail. Students will also learn guidelines and safety practices in the storage, preparation, and safe disposal of anesthetic agents. Effects of anesthesia agents in specialized populations, including elderly and children will also be discussed. Prerequisites: ANT 240; ANT 245.

ANT 343L.title: Operating Room Simulation Lab

ANT 343L.description: This immersive and simulation-based high-fidelity course provides anesthesia technology students with the opportunity to demonstrate clinical applications of anesthesia in a simulated operating room environment. In the mock operating room, control room, and debriefing room, students will be taught to use their knowledge and critical thinking in a variety of case scenarios. Simulations will include the pre- operative assessment of the patient, preparation of the anesthetic plan, induction, maintenance, and emergence phases of anesthesia. This course also offers an opportunity for students to train on practicing vigilance in the delivery of patient care, developing their decision-making skills, and interpersonal dynamics. Prerequisite: ANT 240L.

ANT 360.title: Perioperative Patient Care
notices: Taken from the College of Healthcare Technology curriculum (Anesthesia Technology, Appendices VII and VIII). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
ANT 360.description: This course aims to provide students with the knowledge required in the assessment and care of patients during the preoperative, operative and postoperative process. After learning about postoperative complications, students will learn to assess risks by performing a preoperative evaluation of the patient by collecting medical history information and using physical exams, including cardiac, airways exams, and the Mallampati Score. Signs of perioperative complications associated with chronic illnesses such as cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, and renal deficiency will be identified and management strategies will be detailed. In addition to preoperative assessment, students will learn intraoperative and postoperative interventions. This course also provides students with a working knowledge of devices and equipment used in the peri-operative clinical monitoring of patients. Prerequisite: ANT 240.

Multimodal analgesia will be described in detail including classes of systemic analgesic medications, uses, doses, routes of administration, and their importance in controlling over-reliance on opioids. The use of preventive analgesia in the control of central sensitization will also be addressed in detail. Prerequisite: ANT 340.

ANT 430L.description: This course takes place in the anesthesia simulation laboratory and aims to test the students on 1) their knowledge of a variety of guidelines including the most updated pre-anesthesia checkout procedures and the safety guidelines established by the Quality Management and Departmental Administration (QMDA) of the American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) and other standardized quality management guidelines, and 2) an array of case scenarios that require quality improvement. ARC 100.title: Introduction to Ancient Near Eastern Archaeology
ARC 100.description: An overview of the ancient Near East, this course examines its history, geography, art, and architecture. Beginning with the development of agriculture in the Neolithic period, it traces the rise of urban societies in Iraq and the great empires of Mesopotamia, Assyria, Babylonia, and Sumer. Thematic topics include culture, politics, writing, religion, and gender roles. Attention is also given to neighboring civilizations such as the Achaemenid Empire, Anatolia, the Hittites, Egypt, and the Phoenicians.

ARC 101.title: Introduction to Heritage Studies
ARC 101.description: This course examines representation of indigenous cultures in the heritage narrative. It maps heritage studies within history, archaeology, tourism, sociology, anthropology, economics, development, philosophy, international relations, and law. It discusses contested heritage notions, restitution and repatriation of estranged heritage, and the importance of the heritage discourse to nation-building and social cohesion.

ARC 102.title: Introduction to Cultural Anthropology
ARC 102.description: This course covers key aspects of cultural anthropology, including kinship, religion, language, race, ethnicity, economics, politics, and sustainability, while also highlighting the ethical considerations of ethnographic research. Students will gain insights essential to understanding our interconnected world, fostering sensitivity to social differences, and enhancing awareness of diverse human experiences.

BDS 340.title: Endodontics I
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 340.description: This lecture course gives the student a clear understanding of the biological foundations of pulpal and periapical diseases and discusses the causes and progression of these problems. BDS 340L.title: Preclinical Endodontics I
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 340L.description: This preclinical course simulates clinical experience and skill development of therapeutic techniques already shown in the lecture course. Both extracted and artificial teeth mounted in simulated mannequin patients are used to prepare the student to apply endodontic care to the patients. Course Prerequisite or Corequisite: BDS 340

BDS 341.title: Endodontics II
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 341.description: This course is a continuity of BDS 340; it addresses endodontic treatment related to multirooted teeth, root canal preparation, disinfection, and obturation techniques. Course Prerequisite: BDS 340.

BDS 341L.title: Preclinical Endodontics II
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 341L.description: This preclinical course simulates clinical experience and skill development of therapeutic techniques already shown in the lecture course. BDS 360.title: Operative Dentistry I
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 360.description: This lecture courses will give foundation knowledge of operative instrumentation, operative dentistry terminology, principles of cavity preparations, and the basics of single tooth restorations and esthetic restoration. Course Prerequisite: BDS 200 and BDS 260.

BDS 360L.title: Preclinical Operative Dentistry I
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 360L.description: This hands-on simulated clinic course provides demonstrations, experience and skill development with the procedures related to direct intracoronal, esthetic tooth restorations. The students will work also on simulators. Course Prerequisite: BDS 360.

BDS 361.title: Operative Dentistry II
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 361.description: This lecture course is a continuity of Operative dentistry I, and give advanced knowledge on intracoronal and indirect esthetic restoration. Course Prerequisite: BDS 360.

BDS 361L.title: Preclinical Operative Dentistry II
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 361L.description: This hands-on simulated clinic course is a continuity of BDS 360 L, it provides demonstrations, experience and skill development with the procedures related to indirect intracoronal, esthetic tooth restorations. The students will work also on simulators. Course Prerequisite or Corequisite: BDS 361.

BDS 370.title: Oral Medicine I
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 370.description: Lectures and case presentations in this course illustrate methods of clinical diagnosis of oral and systemic diseases. Treating oral mucosal lesions, oral manifestations of systemic diseases and their effects on comprehensive oral health care is discussed according to each oral lesion or disease. It will stress on oro-facial pain and the concept of immunity as related to oro-facial lesions including AIDS. Course Prerequisite: BDS 230.

BDS 372.title: Radiology and Radioprotection
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 372.description: This course introduces basic radiology concepts to undergraduate dental students. Students will gain knowledge of the basic concepts of how x-rays are created and interact, as well as a familiarity with dental radiographic techniques. In addition, this course includes training students to analyze the biological effects of ionizing radiation and to apply current radioprotection measures. Course Prerequisite: BDS 200.

BDS 380.title: Periodontology I
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 380.description: This course presents the clinical and microscopic characteristics of the periodontium in healthy and diseased states. Diagnosis, risk factors, non-surgical periodontal treatment, and outcomes assessment are discussed. Course Prerequisite: BDS 230.

BDS 380L.title: Preclinical Hygiene, Ergonomics & Periodontics
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 380L.description: This course is designed to introduce students to basic concepts and skills necessary for the successful practice of dentistry. Concepts include didactic instruction in the following areas: infection control, bacterial plaque formation, etiology and prevention of both dental caries and periodontal disease and patient education for both individual and group instruction. Clinical instruction is provided in the Predoctoral Treatment Center and Simulation Learning Center. It focuses on instruction in infection control, patient evaluation, and basic instrumentation skills. Course Prerequisite or Corequisite: BDS 380.

BDS 402.title: Evidence-Based Dentistry
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 402.description: This course will allow the students to assess and evaluate published scientific and dental literature. Students learn to examine the general concepts in experimental design, scientific methodology, and the appropriateness of statistical methods used to evaluate the conclusions of studies. Some sessions are dedicated to help the students develop sound reasoning and critical thinking skills, the student will work in small groups and led by faculty members. Students will analyze scientific literature and learn about general patterns of clinical judgment, critical thinking, decision-making, and application of scientific evidence into everyday practice. Course Prerequisite: BDS 240.

BDS 404.title: Medical Emergencies in Dentistry
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 404.description: Patient history and physical examination are described, along with the prevention and management of medical emergencies in the dental office. Course Prerequisite: BDS 302.

BDS 406.title: Implant dentistry
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 406.description: This course presents the scientific basis for diagnosis, treatment planning, surgical protocol, and prosthetic options in modern dental Implantology. Course Prerequisite: BDS 380 and BDS 320.

BDS 410.title: Implant prosthodontics
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 410.description: Students will gain knowledge of the principles of fixed and removable restorations over dental implants. Course Prerequisite: BDS 311.

BDS 410C.title: Clinical Operative & Prosthodontics
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 410C.description: During this clinical course students will perform examination and diagnostic procedures, comprehensive treatment planning, all restorative dental procedures, fixed and removable prosthodontic procedures. Course Prerequisite: BDS 311.

BDS 410L.title: Preclinical Fixed Prosthodontics III
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 410L.description: This simulated preclinical course provides practical experience and skill development for restoring missing and/or badly broken-down teeth by fabricating non-removable prostheses. Students will work on single-tooth crowns and multiple-tooth bridgework on plastic tooth models and simulating phantom heads. Students will gain hands-on experience in fixed prosthodontics and occlusion's clinical and technical aspects. Course Prerequisite or Corequisite: BDS 410.

BDS 412L.title: Preclinical Implant prosthodontics
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 412L.description: The course is a combination of didactic classroom learning and simulated lab exercises. The course will prepare the students to restore patients in a clinical setting using dental implants as a treatment option. They will perform digital impressions of the dentition, learn how to fabricate an accurate surgical guide for its use in guided surgery, restore dental implants on a model, and restore overdentures supported by dental implants. Course Prerequisite: BDS 410.

BDS 420.title: Oral Surgery II
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 420.description: This course is a continuity of Oral surgery I. It stresses basic concepts of wound healing, hemostasis control, and postoperative care. Case presentations of major oral surgical procedures are shown and discussed. Course Prerequisite: BDS 320.

BDS 420C.title: Clinical Oral Surgery I
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 420C.description: Students perform uncomplicated exodontia and minor pre-prosthetic surgical procedures that the clinical instructors approve. They will assist the instructors in complicated surgical procedures. Student's clinical experience will be delivered in recurrent 2-week blocks during the semester. This type of experience will give students a better understanding of delivering surgical care by having more hands-on experience, as they will be able to follow up on the recovery of individual patients. Course Prerequisite: BDS 420.

BDS 430.title: Removable Prosthodontics II
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 430.description: This lecture course addresses complete denture construction. Design of these prostheses including an in-depth discussion of denture occlusion. Fabrication, Insertion, adjustment, and correction of these prostheses. Course Prerequisite: BDS 330.

BDS 430L.title: Preclinical Removable Prosthodontics II
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.

Course Prerequisite or Corequisite: BDS 430.

BDS 440.title: Endodontics III
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 440.description: This lecture course address main endodontic treatment management, pain control, pharmacotherapeutics, treatment of trauma cases and uncompleted roots, and advanced therapeutic endodontic treatment. Course Prerequisite: BDS 341.

BDS 440C.title: Clinical Endodontics I
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 440C.description: This course is a clinical training dedicated to root canal treatment on monoradicular teeth. Course Prerequisite or Corequisite: BDS 341.

BDS 440L.title: Preclinical Endodontics III
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 440L.description: This preclinical course simulates clinical experience and skill development of therapeutic techniques already shown in BDS 440. Both extracted and artificial teeth mounted in simulated mannequin patients are used to prepare the student to apply endodontic care to the patients. Course Prerequisite or Corequisite: BDS 440.

BDS 450C.title: Comprehensive Care and General Dentistry I
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 450C.description: Comprehensive care is defined as the overall patient care delivery system that includes all dental services, including emergency care, treatment planning, general dentistry, specialty care, implant-supported restorations, non-surgical periodontal procedures, and maintenance therapy. Under supervision, the student will perform clinical general dental practice for adult patients. Patients and case discussions in the form of seminars are included. The student's knowledge and practical skills will be assessed by the supervisors during clinical practice. To "Pass" this course, the students must have done a number of required clinical work. Course Prerequisite or Corequisite: BDS 410C.

BDS 470.title: Oral Medicine II
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 470.description: This lecture course is a continuity of Oral Medicine I; it emphasizes congenital and hereditary disorders involving tissues of the orofacial region, salivary glands disorders, and tongue in oral and systemic diseases. This course aims to develop students' competency using critical thinking and problem-solving related to the comprehensive care of patients with oral diseases. Course Prerequisite: BDS 370.

BDS 470C.title: Clinical Oral Diagnosis & Oral Medicine & Radiology
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 470C.description: This clinical course will allow the students to assist in diagnosing oral conditions and discuss treatment options and strategies. Course Prerequisite: BDS 470.

BDS 472.title: Radiology
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 472.description: This course presents advanced imaging techniques including extraoral imaging, panoramic imaging and digital imaging. Lectures and case presentations will prepare the students to analyze radiographs and be proficient in interpretation of caries, periodontal disease and periapical pathology. The students will also gain knowledge of the radiographic features of various jaw diseases including cysts, tumors, fibro-osseous lesions, systemic disease, infections and developmental diseases affecting the oral tissues. Course Prerequisite: BDS 372.

BDS 480.title: Periodontology II
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 480.description: This course continues the discussion of concepts presented in the previous Periodontology I course. Emphasis is placed on the diagnosis and clinical management of periodontal disease, including the principles and techniques of periodontal surgery. Course Prerequisite: BDS 380.

BDS 480C.title: Clinical Periodontics I
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 480C.description: This clinical course emphasizes the non-surgical treatment of the patient's existing gum disease and the maintenance of healthy periodontium through patient education. Course Prerequisite: BDS 480.

BDS 490.title: Pediatric Dentistry
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 490.description: The course focuses on training in patient management, preventive and restorative dentistry, diagnosis and management of common pediatric problems, and treatment of traumatic dental injuries. This course also discusses the development and growth of the orofacial structures of the child and adolescent. Course Prerequisite: BDS 361.

BDS 490L.title: Preclinical Pediatric-Orthodontic dentistry
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 490L.description: This course is a comprehensive simulated clinic introduction to the techniques of pediatric dentistry and orthodontic techniques. It includes the technical aspects of restorative dentistry and space maintenance. Course Prerequisite or Corequisite: BDS 490 - BDS 495.

BDS 495.title: Orthodontics
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 495.description: This lecture course discusses concepts in the growth and development of the craniofacial complex, the diagnosis, etiology, and development of malocclusions with a special focus on their diagnosis and multidisciplinary treatment planning. Intervention in growth problems for children and minor tooth movement for adults are included, as well as access to Invisalign and aligners technology. Course Prerequisite: BDS 472.

BDS 502.title: Ethics in Dentistry
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 502.description: This course builds the student's understanding and consideration of ethical issues in dental practice and introduces related legal principles. Through lecture and case discussion, the student will focus on ethical problem-solving in more complex patient-based cases and introduces legal concepts affecting the practice of dentistry including licensure, malpractice, informed consent and refusal, mandatory reporting laws, patient confidentiality and prudent behavior, diversity and discrimination laws. Course Prerequisite: BDS 404.

BDS 504.title: Geriatric Dentistry
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 504.description: This course integrates biomedical, clinical, and behavioral science principles into the evaluation and treatment planning of older adults and adults with special needs. This course focuses on patient-centered ways to promote, improve, maintain, and modify oral health care. This course also provides opportunities for critical thinking and foundational knowledge regarding interprofessional care and referrals, the social and behavioral implications of aging, polypharmacy, and management of oral health and quality of life for medically compromised older adults and adults living with special needs. Course Prerequisite: BDS 430.

BDS 520.title: Current Development in Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 520.description: This lecture-based course is designed to give the student exposure to all aspects of the wide and varied scope of oral and maxillofacial surgery. The course also promotes the integration of the basic sciences and medicine into the daily practice of oral and maxillofacial surgery and dentistry. Course Prerequisite: BDS 420C.

BDS 540C.title: Clinical Endodontics II
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 540C.description: This course is a clinical training dedicated to root canal treatment on monoradicular and biradicular teeth. Course Prerequisite: BDS 440C.

BDS 542C.title: Clinical Endodontics III
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 542C.description: Student's clinical experiences consist of diagnosing and treating pulpal and periapical dental pathology requiring endodontic intervention. This course focuses on case selection, specialty referral, non-surgical root canal therapy, emergency endodontic treatment, and clinical endodontic procedures of monoradicular and multiradicular teeth. Course Prerequisite: BDS 540C.

BDS 550C.title: Comprehensive Care and General Dentistry II
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 550C.description: This clinical training is a continuity of Comprehensive care and general dentistry I. The student will have to manage more complex treatment cases. The students' knowledge and practical skills will be assessed by the supervisors during clinical practice. To "Pass" this course the students must have done a number of required clinical work. Course Prerequisite: BDS 450C.

BDS 552C.title: Community Dental Practice
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 552C.description: Clinical experiences allow students to apply knowledge and develop competencies related to oral health promotion and disease prevention activities with individual patients. This course also provides the students with experience in treating diverse patient populations. Students might be assigned to alternative treatment settings such as Community Health Centers or Hospital-based dental clinics. Course Prerequisite or Corequisite: BDS 450C.

BDS 554C.title: Treatment Planning and Case Presentations
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 554C.description: This Faculty supervised course comprises clinical case presentations, case-based learning, and treatment planning seminars. Through these activities, students learn skills to evaluate a patient's needs and develop an orderly, prioritized, and sequential course of problem-based treatment. The student learns to present this information in a way that enables the patient to conceptualize what treatment he or she requires and to co-participate in an informed fashion in developing their treatment plan. Students should develop realistic goals and expectations for patients and dentists through participation in this course. The seminar presentation requires a conversation about the patient's medical or physical condition demonstrating the student's knowledge of biomedical science. The students are required to support a treatment concept, procedure, or material choice proposed in their patient's therapy and support their decisions based on the available evidence in the dental literature. Students will prepare case presentations delivered via PowerPoint to other students and subjected to questions and debate; they will demonstrate their communication skills and comprehensive understanding of the presented material before peers and Faculty. Course Prerequisite: BDS 550C.

BDS 556C.title: Comprehensive care and general dentistry III
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 556C.description: This clinical training is a continuity of Comprehensive care and general dentistry II. The student will have to manage more complex treatment cases. The students' knowledge and practical skills will be assessed by the supervisors during clinical practice. To "Pass" this course the students must have done a number of required clinical work. Course Prerequisite: BDS 550C

BDS 570.title: Oral Medicine III
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 570.description: This lecture course is a continuity of Oral Medicine II, it emphasizes on congenital and hereditary disorders involving tissues of orofacial region, cysts, neoplasms, odontomes and fibro-osseous lesions, forensic odontology, premalignant and malignant lesion of orofacial region. This course aims to develop students' competency using critical thinking and problem-solving related to the comprehensive care of patients with oral diseases. Course Prerequisite: BDS 470C.

BDS 570C.title: Radiology and Digital Dentistry
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 570C.description: Based on current literature, this course will review current techniques for incorporating intraoral scanners, 3D CBCT imaging, and CAD/CAM Technology into your everyday practice. Students will rotate between the radiology and the planning rooms; they will be asked to read CBCT scans and treatment plans and, in some cases, do digital smile design. Course Prerequisite: BDS 472.

BDS 590C.title: Clinical Pediatric Dentistry I
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 590C.description: This course includes Pediatric Dentistry, where students receive preventive and restorative dentistry training, treatment planning, and behavior management. Course Prerequisite or Corequisite: BDS 490.

BDS 592C.title: Clinical Pediatric Dentistry II
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 592C.description: This clinical training is a continuity course of Clinical Pediatric Dentistry I. Students will be trained under supervision for treating pediatric Special Needs patients for preventive and restorative dentistry, treatment planning, and behavior management. They will do rotation training to treat traumatic dental injuries at the children's dentistry clinics. Course Prerequisite: BDS 590C.

BDS 595C.title: Clinical Orthodontics I
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 595C.description: The student will have clinical experience in assisting Faculty providing patients with orthodontic treatment. This clinical training will focus on clinical diagnosis and radiographic evaluation of patients seeking orthodontic treatment. Course Prerequisite: BDS 495.

BDS 597C.title: Clinical Orthodontics II
notices: Taken from the College of Dentistry academic curriculum (BDS). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDS 597C.description: This clinical course is a continuity of clinical orthodontics I, it allows the student to gain more experience in diagnosis, and referral of orthodontic patients. Course Prerequisite: BDS 595C.

BDT 210.title: Dental Material I
notices: Taken from the College of Healthcare Technology curriculum (Dental Technology, Appendices V and VI). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDT 210.description: The present course is designed for students to define and recite an appropriate overview of the basic knowledge of the physical, chemical, and mechanical properties of materials used in different branches of dentistry. Also, the students can determine all fundamentals knowledge of polymer, metals, and ceramics to bridge the gap between the obtained basic knowledge and the clinical dental operatory. Course Prerequisite: CHE 105.

BDT 210L.title: Dental Material lab
notices: Taken from the College of Healthcare Technology curriculum (Dental Technology, Appendices V and VI). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDT 210L.description: This laboratory course is a continuity of Dental material I. The students will acquire and practical data about restorative dental materials as regards to their manipulation, properties, for lab and clinical application. Course Prerequisite or Corequisite: BDT 210.

BDT 211.title: Dental Materials II
notices: Taken from the College of Healthcare Technology curriculum (Dental Technology, Appendices V and VI). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDT 211.description: This course is a continuity of Dental materials I. The course is also directed to enable students to make rational decisions on properly selecting dental materials and their use relying on evidence-based dentistry. Course Prerequisite or Corequisite: BDT 210.

BDT 320.title: Fixed Prosthodontics I

BDT 320.description: Fixed Prosthodontics I. Listed in the College of Healthcare Technology curriculum (Dental Technology, Appendices V and VI), which gives no description.

BDT 320L.title: Fixed Prosthodontics lab I

BDT 330.title: Partial Denture Prosthodontics I

The procedures of design, duplicating, waxing, investing, casting, and finishing will be developed. Then the arrangement and processing of artificial teeth and the repairing of frameworks will be introduced. Prerequisite: BDT 211.

BDT 330L.title: Removable Prosthodontics lab I
notices: Taken from the College of Healthcare Technology curriculum (Dental Technology, Appendices V and VI). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDT 330L.description: This course will give students practical knowledge in the fabrication of removable prosthesis. It will allow students to develop their technical skills through construction of partial and complete dentures. Course Prerequisite: BDT 330.

BDT 331L.title: Removable Prosthodontics lab II
notices: Taken from the College of Healthcare Technology curriculum (Dental Technology, Appendices V and VI). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDT 331L.description: This course is a continuity of Removable Prosthodontics lab I, it will give students advanced practical knowledge in the fabrication of removable prosthesis. Course Prerequisite: BDT 330L.

BDT 340.title: Complete Denture Prosthodontics I
notices: Taken from the College of Healthcare Technology curriculum (Dental Technology, Appendices V and VI). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDT 340.description: An introduction to the setup and arrangement of artificial teeth. Waxing, investing, processing, and finishing procedures will also be taught. The basics of denture repair will be introduced. Prerequisite: BDS 200.

BDT 350.title: Dental ceramics
notices: Taken from the College of Healthcare Technology curriculum (Dental Technology, Appendices V and VI). This course is not in the SIS course catalog yet, so confirm it with the college.
BDT 350.description: Ceramic materials have evolved significantly during the past decades along with their fabrication techniques, and all-ceramic restorations have gained in popularity. This course will give laboratory technicians complete knowledge of the properties and characteristics of ceramics in order to select the most appropriate restorative materials for each case. BUS 112.title: Introduction to Business

Students will learn the essential components of the business world and the organizations that exist in it. Students will discover why location is such a significant force in society and prepare themselves for careers in the business sector. Prerequisite: ASP level five.

BUS 212.title: Professional Development and Career Planning
BUS 212.description: This course is designed to improve your understanding of professional development (PD) and career planning (CD). By combining theory, research, and practice, we will examine key topics related to PD & CD, such as the framework for understanding PD & CD, developing and practicing career-enhancing skills, and functions of career planning (e.g., mentoring and coaching personnel and conducting career assessments). Prerequisite: BUS 112.

BUS 215.title: Business Law
notices: This course has not been scheduled.
BUS 215.description: This course is an introductory course dealing with legal principles and procedures. It is an introduction to contract law. The main objective of this course is to introduce students to business transactions and to develop an understanding of the legal framework of business- the basic principles of the law which form the legal framework for business activity including applicable statutes, contracts, and agency. The course will equip students with the necessary knowledge to choose the form of business entity, structure ownership, raise money, handle operational liabilities, protect intellectual property, go global, and go public. Special attention will be given to Iraqi Company Law No. 21 as amended in 2004 which aims at protecting creditors from fraud, protect shareholders from conflicts of interest.

BUS 250.title: Business Statistics
BUS 250.description: Business Statistics is a critical tool for decision-making in business and economic situations. Students will learn the basics of data description, ideas associated with probability distributions, and inferential techniques, including confidence intervals and hypothesis testing for parameter values. Concepts of linear regression will be introduced through line fitting to bivariate data. Prerequisite: BUS 112.

BUS 375.title: Internship

Internships offer the opportunity to “try out” a career while gaining relevant experience and professional connections. Internships are completed under the guidance of an on-site supervisor and a faculty sponsor, who, in combination with the student, will create a framework for learning and reflection. ENT 310.title: Foundations of Entrepreneurship I: Business Discovery and Assessment
ENT 310.description: This course introduces students to the foundational process of discovering and evaluating viable new business opportunities. Rather than relying on entrepreneurial intuition, the course emphasizes a structured, iterative approach used by successful entrepreneurs to identify market openings, assess organizational capabilities, and determine whether a venture can create and capture value. Students learn how to evaluate industry conditions, analyze value creation, and assess the financial feasibility of proposed ventures. Through case studies and student-driven projects, participants apply these concepts to real business ideas. The course culminates in a comprehensive business feasibility study. It is designed for both aspiring business students interested in entrepreneurship and non-business students seeking innovative ways to create sustainable opportunities in their chosen fields. Prerequisite: MGT 201.

ENT 320.title: Foundations of Entrepreneurshi
ENT 320.description: The main focus of this course is to consider and discuss entrepreneurial processes in established firms as well as newly created ventures. It focuses less on the 'how' of entrepreneurship, but on the 'what' and the 'why'. It considers theories on the nature of entrepreneurship that explain entrepreneurial success and how entrepreneurship relates to innovation. Over the course of the semester, students will work in teams to work on case studies, culminating in an end-of-term individual case development and presentation. Students work individually or in groups to launch an opportunity business as a minimum viable product (MVP) related to Baghdad-area industries. Success is measured in launching an MVP, gathering customer feedback, and pitching to guest investors. Prerequisite: ENT 310.

LAW 101.title: Introduction to the Study of Law (Law Theory; Right Theory):
LAW 101.description: This course is introductory. The course aims to provide a basic but fundamental understanding of the nature of law, legal rules, legal persons, and legal rights. The course topics include the concept, characteristics, and functions of legal rules, the division or branches of law, sources of law, and the interpretation and application of legal rules. This course also deals with legal personality and classification of legal rights (civil rights, property rights, human rights, etc.). Language of Instruction: English.

LAW 102.title: Legal Terminology
LAW 102.description: The course covers legal English's key vocabulary and emphasizes legal terms used in legal courses in the College of Law. The course emphasizes the mastery of legal vocabulary to enhance students' proficiency in legal communication across multiple areas of law. The course also provides basic instruction in legal principles, including contracts, torts, legal procedure, constitutional law, and administrative law. LAW 103.title: Legal Reasoning and Writing
LAW 103.description: This course teaches students to make professional legal writing decisions and to think and argue simultaneously like a lawyer or legal adviser. The act of writing requires a law professional to test, analyze, structure, and express thoughts and ideas with clarity and precision. This course examines basic concepts of law and legal reasoning. The course focuses on the writing process and how to use language as a professional tool. Students are introduced to several types of written legal documents, including predictive writing and persuasive writing. Students also learn to “brief” cases and prepare memoranda of law, appellate briefs, and client communication. Language of Instruction: English. Prerequisites / Corequisites: LAW 101 and LAW 102.

LAW 104.title: Criminology and Penology
LAW 104.description: This course provides students with an introduction and overview of the system of criminal justice in operation. The course begins with a survey of the sources, philosophy, and role of law in society, and provides a brief introduction to different legal traditions and systems. The course also examines those factors that distinguish civil, criminal, and social justice. Students learn the definitions of a "crime", “evidence,” and social responses to crimes. A broad survey of the policing and prosecution, Adjudication, sentencing, and corrections provide students with a basic understanding of the administration of criminal justice. Language of Instruction: English. Adjudication, sentencing, and corrections provide students with a basic understanding of the administration of criminal justice. Language of Instruction: English. Course Prerequisites: None.

LAW 105.title: Introduction to Islamic Law (Sharia)
notices: This course has not been scheduled.
LAW 105.description: This course familiarizes students with the sources, nature, and functions of Islamic law in a historical context. It provides a framework for thinking about social realities and institutional structures that help shape Islamic law and explains the legal adaptations within Islamic law over time. The power, history, and theory of the Islamic Legal System are examined with particular emphasis on the development of the various schools of thought within Islamic law, and the interaction between the Sharia and recently promulgated Civil Codes. This course also encourages comparative legal analysis to assess generalizations about law typically formulated by Western legal traditions. Language of Instruction: Arabic.

LAW 106.title: Constitutional Law
LAW 106.description: This course is divided into three parts. The first part examines the general constitutional theories of diverse states and political systems (Theories of States). Part two examines the nature of constitutions, a survey of the US, French, and EU constitutions, as well as the relationships among the executive, legislative, and judicial areas of government. Constitutional principles, rights, and civil liberties are also discussed, considering the long tradition of diverse philosophical and theoretical perceptions (Theories of Constitutions or Constitutionalism). Part three of the course examines the history, formation, basic principles, and structure of the Iraqi constitution, including its current application. The theories and practices of judicial review and federal and unitary states are also discussed. Language of Instruction: English & Arabic. Prerequisites / Corequisites: LAW 101 and LAW 102.

LAW 112.title: History of Roman Law and Hammurabi Law
LAW 112.description: Contemporary laws emerge from the long-term development of diverse legal systems, and a variety of sources and conceptions of law. Historically, the Romano-Germanic legal system is the group of legal ideas and systems ultimately derived from the core principles of the Code of Justinian. This course examines Rome’s political and legal system, the legal status of the individual in Roman Law, and the rules that regulate financial relations in Roman Law. The course also examines Hammurabi's Law, which reflected legal articles from multiple legal systems (public Law and Private Law). In particular, the sources and key features of Hammurabi Law, as well as the relevant governance and administrative systems, financial and commercial legislation, and the penal system. Language of Instruction: English. Prerequisites / Corequisites: LAW101 and LAW102.

LAW 220.title: Civil Law (Obligations Theory)
LAW 220.description: This course aims to provide students with an understanding of the foundational principles of ‘obligations’ in the Civil Law and Common Law System from a comparative perspective. The course examines the concepts employed in creating and enforcing different types of obligations. Students will be able to differentiate between the sources and foundations of obligations in contract and delict/tort in Private Law, and identify the essential elements of the formation of contracts and certain other requirements (form and content), which must be satisfied to make contracts legally enforceable. Vitiating factors, such as avoidance, discharge, termination, and remedies for breach, are also discussed. The course investigates unilateral contract/legal transactions and non-contractual liability, specifically the delictual/tortuous liability resulting from the wrongful/harmful acts of others. The course discusses theoretical foundations, analyzes legal issues, and presents hypothetical scenarios to promote student participation and active engagement in the learning process. Language of Instruction: English & Arabic. Prerequisites / Corequisites: LAW 101.

LAW 221.title: Administrative Law
LAW 221.description: This course provides students with an understanding of the foundational concepts and principles of administrative law and public administration. The development and evolution of administration in civil as well as common law countries is explained. The course also provides an understanding of how administrative law functions and allows students to dissect the characteristics of administrative law, the forms and functions of administrative organizations, and the classification and objectives of administrative actions. Key concepts and issues, such as administrative contracts and public utilities, the legal personality of administrative organs, and types and limitations of administrative control, are covered. The course investigates the methods of administrative decision-making as well as their implementation and enforcement in practice. Language of Instruction: English and Arabic. Prerequisite / Corequisite: LAW106.

LAW 224.title: Civil Law (Provisions of Obligations)
LAW 224.description: This course builds on the understanding of civil law obligations provided in the course LAW 220, specifically by focusing on legal provisions in the Iraqi Civil Code of 1951. The course provides a brief reflection on the formation of a contract and its essential elements. It then discusses in detail the effects and dissolution of the contract. The course provides a brief reflection on legal provisions relating to unilateral and illegal/prohibited contracts and covers delictual/tortuous liability for ‘unlawful acts and gains without justification (restitution/unjust enrichment). Further, the course deals with conditions and terms in a contract, where each is defined in terms of types, effects, and expiration. The plurality of parties in contract and transfer of obligation, whether by assignment of rights or assignment of debt, are discussed. Finally, the course discusses in detail the discharge of obligation either by way of performance, renewal, delegation, or by impossibility of performance and the statute of limitations. Language of Instruction: English & Arabic. Prerequisite: LAW 220.

LAW 227.title: Personal Status Law (Marriage & Divorce)
LAW 227.description: This course examines topics such as marriage contracts and their purpose, provisions of engagement, terms of the contract and full capacity, lack of capacity, incomplete capacity, forced marriage, registration of the marriage contract, and proof of marriage. Definitions of guardianship in the marriage contract and the reasons for the prohibition in the Marriage contracts are covered. In addition, the course covers matters relating to dowry and women's entitlement to the entire dowry. It also deals with definitions and conditions for divorce and alimony, elements of alimony, and Personal Status Law for Non-Muslims. Language of Instruction: Arabic. Prerequisite: LAW 105. .

LAW 230.title: Criminal Law: General Theory
LAW 230.description: This course deals with defining the concept of crime, explaining classifications of crimes, and distinguishing between criminal offenses, disciplinary offenses, and civil wrongs. The concepts and importance of the rule of law and the principle of legality as they relate to crimes and penalties are discussed. This includes clarification of the principles that govern the application of the Penal Code in terms of place and time and the validity of those rules. Also discussed are the nature and elements of crime -the physical element and the moral element-, including an explanation of attempts to commit a crime and criminal participation in the offense. An examination of the impediments to criminal responsibility and the reasons for legally established permissibility will also be explored. Language of Instruction: English & Arabic. Prerequisite: LAW 104.

LAW 240.title: Human Rights and International Humanitarian Law
LAW 240.description: This course covers various aspects of human rights law, including theories, sources, traditions, and legal guarantees, including the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, Covenants, and third-generation rights. The course deals with regional systems of human rights and contemporary issues around human rights, such as the impact of globalization and new technologies, terrorism, and human rights in Iraq. The first part of the course provides an overview of the prosecution of human rights violations at the international level, specifically at the international criminal courts and tribunals. The course examines the fundamentals of international humanitarian law, specifically the laws of war, rules concerning cyberattacks, and the intersections with human rights law. The course also comprehends the Geneva Conventions, the Rome Statute, and the International Criminal Court, with a focus on mechanisms for the implementation of International Humanitarian Law and the principles of international criminal law. Language of Instruction: English. Prerequisite: LAW 101.

LAW 260.title: Financial Legislation and Tax Law
LAW 260.description: This course provides an overview of Iraqi fiscal policy, domestic tax codes, and related legislation. Because fiscal policy is used to influence the economy, the course covers government borrowing, public debt, and the government’s role in expanding or contracting GDP. The international part of the course focuses on principles of international taxation where enterprises are subject to taxation in more than one Nation State. The Model Tax Convention of the OECD is used to explain jurisdiction to tax, permanent establishment, transfer pricing, and asset classifications. MTC is also used to explain Double Tax Treaties and methods of tax relief, such as exemption and credit. OECD reforms such as BEPS 1.0 and 2.0 are covered, time permitting. The emphasis is upon understanding international tax strategies employed by company groups and the efforts of Nation States to generate tax revenue consistent with the principles of international trade, economic growth, and avoidance of double taxation. Language of Instruction: English and Arabic. Course Prerequisites: LAW 106.

LAW 280.title: Commercial and Corporate Law
LAW 280.description: This course provides a comprehensive understanding of key principles in commercial law, including commercial, transport, and insurance contracts. The course uses the United Nations Convention on the International Sale of Goods as an instance of international law, since Iraq is a signatory to the CISG. Incoterms and documentary credits are defined. The course also covers corporate law, encompassing definitions, types, characteristics, procedural rules, and legal documents governing company formation and registration. Additionally, the course addresses legal issues concerning foreign company branches. Language of Instruction: English and Arabic. Furthermore, the course covers themes like the International Responsibility of States, Diplomatic Protection, and International Succession. Moreover, it addresses peaceful means for resolving international disputes, encompassing the Judicial Settlement of International Disputes, focusing on the International Court of Justice, its composition, and Jurisdiction. Practical sessions related to ICJ case law are also integrated into the course. Language of Instruction: English and Arabic. Prerequisites: Law 240.

LAW 390P.title: Public International law - Problem-Solving
notices: This course has not been scheduled.
LAW 390P.description: This course focuses on training students to gain the skills needed for the Philip C. Jessup Competition and other competitions in the field of international law by teaching previous competition cases. It enables them to understand the fundamentals of international law and the mechanism for solving international problems, as well as develop their skills in writing legal memoranda and pleading for claimants and respondents. the purpose of this course is to prepare students for participation in Philip C. Jessup Competition and others. They gain experience in pretrial, trial, and post-conviction matters under the close supervision of faculty.

LAW 400.title: Labor Law and Social Security
notices: This course has not been scheduled.
LAW 400.description: This course entails a study of general principles in labor legislation in terms of its definition, importance, development, international organization, sources, independence, scope of application of such laws, as well as individual work contracts (elements, duration, termination) and the regulation of collective labor relations and the settlement of labor disputes. This course also deals with Social Security Law, the financial system for social security in Iraq, health insurance, disability, partial disability, and compensation. Language of Instruction: English and Arabic. Prerequisites: LAW 224.

LAW 422.title: Islamic Jurisprudence
notices: This course has not been scheduled.
LAW 422.description: This course deals with the definition of Sharia and jurisprudence, the need for legislation, characteristics, and principles of Islamic jurisprudence and Sharia, the relationship of Sharia with other laws and the law, the history and development of Islamic jurisprudence to the present era, doctrines of jurisprudence and the theory of eligibility and its provisions. This course deals with the definition of the legal ruling: its definition and its divisions, the fundamental rules: general and specific, absolute and restricted, and the theory of interpretation of texts in science Usul al-Fiqh, Ijtihad: Conditions, Place and Ruling. Tradition: its rules and controls, inconsistency. Objectives of Islamic Sharia. Language of Instruction: Arabic. Course Prerequisites: LAW 320.

LAW 431.title: Civil Law: Real Rights and Ancillary
notices: This course has not been scheduled.
LAW 431.description: This course deals with the laws governing all aspects of real property and the creation of rights. Additional topics include ownership rights, real property contracts, real property mortgages, the statute of fraud problems, conveyancing, and adverse possession also discussed as In-kind insurance. Also covered are all aspects of official mortgage contracts, possessory pledges, and franchise rights. Language of Instruction: English and Arabic. Prerequisites: LAW330.

LAW 440.title: Private International Law and
LAW 440.description: This course starts from the general historical development of the doctrines of Private International Law, then covers its relationship with general International Law, general principles of nationality in comparative law, and the state’s freedom to regulate nationality and citizenship. The course also deals with the status of foreigners in terms of the general principles of organizing the legal status of foreigners. The course examines the conflict of laws theory: rules of conflict, classification, and qualification, public policy, and rules of foreign law. recognition and enforcement of foreign judgments, Rules governing international arbitral proceedings, and arbitral jurisdiction. Language of Instruction: English and Arabic. Course Co/Prerequisites: LAW 431, & LAW 390.

LAW 456.title: Criminal Investigation and Forensic
notices: This course has not been scheduled.
LAW 456.description: This course deals with the importance and development of practical criminal investigation, criminal investigatory bodies, their tasks and functions, the characteristics of the criminal investigator, the procedural and substantive rules in the field of investigation and detection of crimes, and the use of legal and technical methods to obtain evidence. The course also aims to introduce how to use various legitimate scientific and technical means in the field of research, investigation of truth, and analysis of effects on crime scenes, whether solid, synthetic, or human gaseous liquid and matching lines. To detect forgery and analyze physical and microscopic traces, hair, fibers, threads, soil, and rocks. It also deals with the definition of auxiliary sciences for forensic sciences such as forensic medicine and its technical foundations, forensic chemistry, especially DNA fingerprinting and fingerprints, and how to deal with various cases such as miscarriage, sudden death, injuries, and their types, and burns. And their types, sexual crimes, personality investigation, drowning suffocation, wounds, burns, and their degree, and the causes of various injuries that lead to death or disability, forgery, counterfeiting, poison, and drugs. Language of Instruction: English. Course Prerequisites: LAW 354, Co/requisites LAW 455.

LAW 460.title: Practicum
LAW 460.description: This course integrates academic theory with practical applications, emphasizing case studies and hands-on projects in diverse legal fields. Designed for AUIB students, visiting students, and legal practitioners alike, it offers a flexible selection of courses to accommodate individual schedules and interests. Some suggested courses are Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR), Women and International Human Rights, and Principles of Legislative Drafting in Law. Language of instruction: Arabic and English. Course Prerequisites: Completion of 60 credits.

LAW 461.title: Commercial Papers and Banking
LAW 461.description: This course introduces the student to the most important principles of commercial law, commercial contracts, banking operations, and the provisions of private companies and public companies. It also covers the procedural rules related to the preparation of corporate contracts and how to register them. The course will also deal with the definition of commercial papers and their types, the bill of exchange, promissory note and check, and knowledge of the provisions of each of them in terms of creating the paper, the commitment of the signatories to it, its circulation, its acceptance, the payment of its value, how the holder returns to the obligors of the commercial paper and the fall of the lawsuits resulting from it by prescription. The course also explores key aspects of banking law, including banking operations and services, the role of banks in issuing, accepting, and processing commercial papers, banking regulations, and compliance, and the relationship between banks and their customers in commercial transactions. Language of Instruction: English and Arabic. Prerequisites: LAW 280.

LAW 499.title: Capstone
LAW 499.description: The Capstone Seminar is a seminar in which students utilize the knowledge and skills gained through their law degree program studies to create a culminating work that critically addresses a problem in a field of law of their choosing. The students produce a Capstone of 3000-5000 words that presents a position on a relevant legal problem, supports the position with legal literature, analyzes and tests the proposed solution, and discusses the finding. Each student will be assigned a faculty member to provide the student with guidance and feedback during the process. Language of Instruction: English. Course Prerequisites: Completion 103 credits.

LDR 640.title: Leadership
LDR 640.description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of leadership theories, styles, and practices. Students will critically evaluate leadership approaches in diverse organizational contexts and develop their own leadership philosophy. The course emphasizes ethical leadership, influence, motivation, and building high-performing teams. Prerequisites: MGT 600 (Recommended) Key Topics: • Leadership theories and models • Leadership styles and behaviors • Motivation and influence • Ethical and responsible leadership • Leading teams and organizations • Leadership development and self-awareness
